lines: Drum trigger sequencer: up to 25 named phrases of drum notes across ten voices, with per-note velocity, accents, ratchets, flams and probability, edited in a popup piano roll
The clock that drives playback, at four ticks per beat, which a clock module calls x4 or 1/16th
Chooses which of the 25 phrases plays, C3 selecting the first and the 25 semitones up to C5 the last; set to trigger on the menu it steps to the next non-empty phrase or picks one at random
A trigger returning the playhead to the beginning, or to the start repeat marker with that option set on the menu; playback carries on immediately if the sequencer is running
A trigger toggling between running and stopped; while stopped the gates are closed and clock ticks are ignored
Returns the playhead to the beginning, or to the start repeat marker with that option set on the menu
Starts and stops playback
Starts and stops recording of the notes arriving at the record inputs into the current phrase
Clears every note out of the current phrase
Records drum notes from a keyboard, the ten white keys from C4 to E5 playing the ten voices
Records drum notes from a General MIDI drum kit, whose standard kit notes are mapped onto the ten voices
The note-on trigger for recording, taken from the gate output of a MIDI-CV module
Sets the velocity of each recorded note
A trigger on each note played by that voice
A trigger on each note of that voice that is marked as an accent in the editor
The velocity of the note being played by that voice
A trigger each time the playhead reaches the end of the phrase
Note — the large display draws the phrase with the playhead as a vertical line, and clicking it opens an editor for adding, moving and deleting notes and setting velocity, accent and probability
Note — the small display names the phrase now playing, and clicking it lists the 25 phrases to choose from
Note — a MIDI file can be imported from the editor or dragged onto it from disk, and the sequence exported to a MIDI file from there
Note — a swing pattern set in the editor offsets quarter, eighth or sixteenth notes forwards or backwards by a chosen fraction, and a pattern set on a narrower part overrides a broader one
Note — with Record enabled and Run switched off, each note played at the record inputs is written at the playhead, which then steps on by the quantisation amount
Note — a new module holds no notes at all and plays nothing; click the large display to open the editor and add notes there, or record them from the record inputs
Note — playback needs a clock patched to the clock input, at four ticks per beat, and the sequencer running; with no clock the playhead does not move and no gate opens
Menu — Phrase selection input — chooses Pitch, C3-C5, Trigger next non-empty phrase, Trigger random phrase (random but fair), or Trigger random phrase (truly random)
Menu — Shared playhead — chooses Don't share the playhead, Shared playhead leader or Shared playhead follower, so several Entrian sequencers move their playheads together
Menu — Delay Clock/Reset/Run inputs — delays those three inputs by Auto, by None, or by a whole number of samples, to make up for the one-sample delay every cable adds
Menu — Set playhead to start marker on reset — sends a reset to the start repeat marker instead of to the beginning
Menu — Stop recording at end of song — ends recording when the playhead reaches the end, without a second press of Record
Menu — Automatically add repeat markers when recording — drops a start marker where recording began and an end marker where it stopped, and the playhead then loops that section
Menu — Save patch to use the free Entrian Player — writes a copy of the patch with every Entrian sequencer replaced by its play-only counterpart from the Entrian Free plugin
Drummer.notes: The panel prints C4-E5 on the voice record input; Entrian's Acoustic Drums page calls it C4-D5, and the panel is followed here because ten white keys starting at C4 end on E5. The Reset and Run output jacks are not described in the manual, on the panel or in the binary, so they are left untagged. The menu item names above were read as literal strings in the binary: 'Phrase selection input:', 'Shared playhead:', 'Delay Clock/Reset/Run inputs', 'Set playhead to start marker on reset', 'Stop recording at end of song', 'Automatically add repeat markers when recording' and 'Save patch to use the free Entrian Player...'. The Light theme and Dark theme items are plugin-wide and cosmetic, so they get no line.

lines: Sampled acoustic drum kit: ten voices drawn from 27 recorded instruments or your own samples, each with several velocity layers, several takes per layer, and a close and a room microphone
Plays a note on that voice each time a trigger arrives
Boosts the volume of the note being triggered on that voice, which also lifts it into the next velocity layer up
Sets how hard that voice is struck; the voltage here is multiplied by the Velocity knob of the same voice
Sets how hard that voice is struck; the knob is multiplied by the voltage at the Velocity input of the same voice
Moves that voice across the stereo picture
Places that voice in the stereo picture, from hard left at one end to hard right at the other
Fades that voice between its close microphone recording and its room microphone recording
Fades that voice between its close microphone recording at one end and its room microphone recording at the other, which is how much room ambience it carries
Shifts the pitch of that voice
Tunes that voice, marked in octaves
That voice on its own, carrying the left channel of its stereo pair, or the whole voice in mono when its Right output is unpatched
The right channel of that voice on its own
The left channel of the ten voices mixed together, or the mono mix when the Right Mix output is unpatched
The right channel of the ten voices mixed together
Note — clicking a voice name opens the list of built-in instruments, the custom sample options, and Instrument options, which holds a gain slider and early decay sliders
Note — Instrument options also chooses, for velocity, pan, distance and tuning, whether a change applies while a note sounds or is frozen at the hit; pan and distance are real time by default
Note — the stepped bar beside each Velocity knob shows the velocity layers that voice was recorded at, and clicking a layer switches it off so that even hard hits use a quieter recording
Note — the Factory presets display offers Close & dry, Balanced, Big room, Laid back and Full on, each of which sets the velocity layers and microphone distance of all ten voices
Note — the hi-hat instruments behave as one physical hi-hat, so a pedal hi-hat chokes a ringing open one; the instrument list also carries independent variants that do not choke
Note — a custom sample is loaded from a WAV or AIFF file; files beside it whose names carry v1, v2 and so on become velocity layers, and r1, r2 and so on become takes within a layer
Note — the module has no sequencer of its own and makes no sound until a trigger arrives at a voice's Trigger input; the ten voices come with a drum kit already assigned
Menu — Include connected instruments in mixed outputs — keeps a voice in the mixed outputs even when its own outputs are patched; switched off, a patched voice is left out of the mix
AcousticDrums.notes: The Tuning CV inputs are given no family: the knob is marked in octaves, but nothing in the manual, the panel or the binary states the scaling of the CV input, so it could not be settled whether it tracks 1V per octave. Knob ranges were read from the factory presets stored in the binary: microphone distance runs -5 to 5, with -5 the close microphone in Close & dry and 5 the room microphone in Full on, and pan is bipolar about zero. The five preset states embedded in the binary all assign an instrument to every one of the ten voices, so a newly added module already has a kit; no sample has to be loaded before it will sound. Drummer has no embedded preset at all, which matches its phrases starting empty.
